To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present a novel C-SLAM method for AUVs communicating only through acustics, which is able to (optimal) generate communication packets that scale linearly with the time since the last successful transmssion, constantly with the size of the collective, and not grow with time in the case of dropped packages, which is common in acoustics.

a graph-based approach to communication-constrained cooperative underwater SLAM can bound the localization error of AUVs and is able to generate packets that scale linearly with the observed features, constantly with the vehicles in the collective and does not grow over time.

a novel graph-based communication-constrained C-SLAM is developed for AUVs that is able to generate communication packets whose sizes scale linearly with the time since the last transmission, and does not depend on the number of features in the map.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing communication-constrained C-SLAM algorithms for AUVs that can be applied in a range of underwater operations.
developing algorithms for multi-robot cooperative operations that can operate under severe communication constraints.
the design and analysis of a C-SLAM approach for multiple AUVs that is able to achieve high accuracy localization and map estimation in the presence of communication constraints.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper proposes a new graph-based C-SALM algorithm that can bound localization error for multiple AUVs operating in an underwater environment with unreliable acoustic communication links.

we have developed a novel algorithm that enables cooperative underwater SLAM for multiple vehicles, which is able to bound the localization error even in the presence of communication errors and dropped packets.
this work presents a new graph-based C-SALM algorithm for multiple AUVs communicating only through acustics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the first time, the C-SLAM problem is formulated in a manner that allows for the communication constraints to be explicitly accounted for in the design of the algorithm.
the paper proposes a graph-based algorithm for cooperative SLAM that is able to generate communication packets that scale optimally in size with the number of robots in the collective.
the presented framework is able to provide a robust and efficient solution for C-SLAM for multi-AUV deployments in challenging environments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed C-SLAM framework can be used to improve the efficiency and reliability of multi-AUV operations.
C-SLAM can be performed in a manner that is robust to communication constraints and can significantly reduce localization error.
, even with very limited communication, cooperative underwater operations are possible and beneficial.
